Marine Spatial Planning
On September 12th, 2025, Ministers O’Brien and Dooley 
announced the publication of the National Designated Maritime 
Area Plan (DMAP) for Offshore Renewable Energy (ORE) Proposal 
and accompanying Public Participation Statement (PPS). 
This announcement formally commenced the preparation of the 
National DMAP for ORE, the aim of which is to designate sites 
in Ireland’s maritime area capable of delivering at least 15GW 
of Offshore Renewable Energy, to be in development by 2040. 
The delivery of this plan is key priority for Government and will 
require a whole of Government approach to be delivered in the 
required timeframe (end 2027). 
The Marine Strategic Policy and Marine Environment and 
Planning sections in the Department of Climate, Energy and the 
Environment (DCEE) are leading the National DMAP development, 
and work is underway on the mapping of ORE opportunity areas 
to identify sites that may be considered potentially feasible for 
ORE. 
The Marine Institute have also compiled a data catalogue to 
enable a comprehensive constraints analysis. The constraints 
analysis process, in addition to focused consultation with 
relevant stakeholders, will allow for further refinement of the 
ORE opportunity areas.
To assist in this process Clare County Council hosted the National 
DMAP team on Thursday the 30th of April as part of their regional 
consultation and engagement on the National DMAP for ORE.
 
Brian Fitzgerald Community Liaison Services for the DMAP process at 
the consultation event. 
The event was well attended by representative groups from Clare 
and Limerick with a morning event having been held earlier in 
the day in Limerick. The event included a presentation from the 
project team on the work carried out to date followed by a briefing 
from the Minister of State at the Department of Environment, 
Climate and Communications Minister Timmy Dooley. A lengthy 
discussion and question and answers session took place following 
the presentations.

Launch of the Quin Community Biodiversity Action Plan
Clare County Council’s Biodiversity Officer presented at the 
launch of the Quin Community Biodiversity Action Plan in 
May 2026. Elected members of Clare County Council were 
also in attendance along with the Minister of State for Nature, 
Biodiversity and Heritage Christopher O’Sullivan who gave the 
keynote address. Students at the local primary school Scoil 
na Mainistreach highlighted their involvement to support 
biodiversity at the ceremony. Among the projects highlighted 
were the biodiversity actions implemented at St. Mary’s Church 
in partnership with Quin Tidy Towns and Clare County Council. 
Actions included establishing a wildflower meadow, swift nest 
box installation on church buildings, planting pollinator friendly 
native trees, installation of barn owl nest boxes with local farmers

National Biodiversity Week 2026
National Biodiversity Week ran from 15th to the 24th of May 2026 
and is organised on an annual basis by the Irish Environmental 
Network (IEN), with support from the Biodiversity Officer 
Network and the National Parks and Wildlife Service. Events are 
run by IEN member groups, as well as by Biodiversity Officers, 
Heritage Officers and other local groups. Clare County Council 
supported several events to celebrate and promote biodiversity 
in County Clare partnering with groups including Hedgerows 
Ireland, Bannergleo, NPWS. Events catered for mixed age groups 
and there was significant interest among the public to learn more 
about biodiversity in their local area.

Inland Fisheries Ireland Barrier Mitigation Fund 
Scheme 2
Inland Fisheries Ireland (IFI) has announced €14.88m in funding 
to support the progression of 91 fish barrier mitigation projects 
nationwide. Nine Clare projects have been awarded funding under 
the scheme. This is the highest number of projects awarded to a 
county alongside Donegal and Meath. The funding is provided 
by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage 
under the National Barrier Mitigation Programme and addresses 
artificial barriers to fish migration. The scheme will support the 
delivery of 91 projects across Ireland. It aims to improve fish 
passage and aquatic habitats, and to restore connectivity in rivers 
and streams. Full details are available to view at the link https://
www.fisheriesireland.ie/news/media-releases/ifi-awards-
almost-eu15m-to-tackle-fish-barriers-nationwide.

Clare Age Friendly Programme 
Reading for Wellness Event
The Reading for Wellness programme was successfully launched 
on 29th April 2026 at Cultúrlann Sweeney Library, Kilkee. The 
event was officially opened by Mayor Paul Murphy, marking a 
significant milestone in promoting mental wellbeing and social 
connection through reading. 
The launch featured a strong line-up of speakers, Cillian Keane 
(Mental Health Ireland), local authors Roisin Meaney and 
Lauretta O’Dea, along with Chairperson Larry Hally from the Clare 
Older People’s Council and the Samaritans. Their contributions 
highlighted the role of reading in supporting relaxation, resilience, 
and reducing social isolation. 
Attendance and engagement at the launch were very positive, 
demonstrating strong community interest. The collaborative 
approach, involving health, community, and literary partners, has 
strengthened the programme’s reach and credibility. Participants 
responded well to the inclusive and welcoming environment, 
with early feedback noting the value of shared reading and 
discussion in supporting wellbeing.
The event was supported by the Clare Age Friendly Programme in 
partnership with Clare Libraries Healthy Clare Libraries.
Celebration of the Bealtaine Festival
The Clare Age Friendly Programme Manager, Clare Age Friendly 
Ambassador, Mike Hanrahan, Clare Arts Officer, Siobhan Mulcahy, 
attended a reception at Áras an Uachtaráin on Thursday, 30 April 
2026. The event was hosted by President Catherine Connolly and 
Mr. Brian McEnery to celebrate the Bealtaine Festival, an Age & 
Opportunity arts initiative recognising the importance of arts and 
creativity as we age.
Their attendance represented the Clare Age Friendly Programme 
and supported engagement at a national level, highlighting the 
importance of age-friendly initiatives and the role of arts and 
culture in promoting positive ageing.
National Network of Older Peoples Council 2026
The Clare Age Friendly Programme Manager, Shanelle Waring, 
and Senior Executive Officer, Leonore O’Neill, attended the Age 
Friendly Ireland National Convention alongside representatives 
of the Clare Older People’s Council, including Larry Hally 
(Chairperson), Mike Cusack (Vice Chair), and Mary Killeen 
McCarthy (member).
On Thursday 7th May (Day 1), the programme commenced 
with formal registration and welcome addresses from Aonghus 
McAnally (Master of Ceremonies), local authority Chief Executives, 
and Anne Drury on behalf of Westmeath Older People’s Council. 
The morning included a national update from Age Friendly 
Ireland and a fireside discussion with senior representatives from 
local government and An Garda Síochána, followed by audience 
engagement. In the afternoon, participants took part in a range 
of workshops and site visits, including sessions on Age Friendly 
public realm and walkability, dementia awareness, community 
preparedness, heritage, and library initiatives. 
On Friday 8th May (Day 2), proceedings included a panel 
discussion on supports for older people, featuring representatives 
from Government departments and national agencies, followed 
by an open question and answer session. Minister of State Kieran 
O’Donnell TD delivered an address, and table discussions explored

priorities for Older People’s Councils in the year ahead. The 
convention concluded with closing remarks, the formal handover 
of the gavel to Clare County Council, and a performance by the 
Sweet Tunes Choir, followed by lunch.
It was noted that Clare will host the National Network of Older 
People’s Councils (NNOPC) Convention in 2027, marking the 
first time Clare will host this national event. Attendance at the 
convention provided valuable opportunities for networking, 
knowledge sharing, and national engagement, supporting the 
continued development of the Clare Age Friendly Programme.
 
Ukrainian Services Team 
Currently, through the Offer a Home Scheme, our Matching & 
Relationship Manager is facilitating the accommodation of 435 
Ukrainian people in 149 units throughout the county. These 
families originally lived in hotel and multi-occupancy facilities. 
The Government has extended the scheme to 31st March 2027 
to align with the EU Temporary Protection Directive. 
Local Authority Integration Team 
The LAIT continues to deliver information and signposting sessions, 
along with Integration Support Clinics, in International Protection 
Accommodation Centres and centres accommodating Ukrainian 
Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection across the county. These 
sessions support residents in accessing essential services and 
provide new community members with the information needed 
to aid their integration into local communities.
 
There are currently 739 Ukrainian Beneficiaries of Temporary 
Protection living in 16 Multi Occupancy state provided 
accommodation Centres in County Clare 
There are currently 959 International Protection applicants living 
in 11 IPAS Centres in County Clare. 
 
On the 13th May Fiona Cahill & Padraig McMahon LAIT 
accompanied the team from Doras & Andrea O’Neill, an 
expert in Mediation & Conflict Resolutions who delivered an 
engaging workshop with the International Protection residents 
in the Burren Castle Hotel who learned valuable tips on how to 
understand, manage and resolve disagreements more effectively.
7th, 12th & 13th May Migrant Voices Recordings took place in 
Scariff with some of the residents from and the Clare Lakelands 
Hotels the East Clare Golf Village who are participating in the 
Migrant Voices Event. This event will be held in June in Scariff 
as part of Refugee week. Participants from Nigeria, Pakistan, 
Zimbabwe, Mauritius, Guatemala and the Ukraine discussed 
some aspects of their new life here in Ireland, cultural differences, 
traditions and memories from their home countries, recording 
was done by Paula Carroll & John Lillis (Clare Memories) and 
Fiona Cahill LAIT accompanied them.
 
14th May Intercultural Food Event collaboration between LAIT, 
LCETB, Ennis Chamber, CISC & CLDC and hosted in the FET 
Campus in Ennis. This event gave people from many different 
countries the opportunity to prepare and share traditional 
dishes from their home cultures, creating a welcoming space for 
cultural exchange, understanding, and social connection within 
the community. This event proved hugely popular and was a fun 
and enjoyable experience for everyone who participated. Some 
of the learners from the FET campus cooked dishes from their 
home countries, people also shared stories which helped to make 
the day such a success.

A new community group, the Ghana Community of Clare, has

Recently, representatives of the group met with the Clare Local

in strengthening safety, trust, and engagement at a local level.

Clare Local Community Safety Plan Update
Work is continuing at pace on the development of the Clare Local 
Community Safety Plan. A countywide survey is currently being 
finalised and will be launched at the June LCSP meeting. Alongside 
this, five targeted surveys are being developed for young people, 
older persons, new and minority communities, and the business 
and farming sectors. A huge thank you to the Working Group for 
their dedication and collaboration in developing these important 
surveys.

Ennis MD - Annual Road Works Programme 
Restoration maintenance of local roads in the Ennis MD 
area in the form of surface dressing commenced this month. 
These roads were identified based on PSCI surveys assessing 
the existing pavement condition, traffic levels and where 
intervention is necessary to avoid structural deterioration taking 
place. Ennis MD assisted with engaging specialist contractors 
while also undertaking preparation works in the form of 
vegetation removal, drainage works and remediating localised 
road defects. Ennis MD in co-ordination with the outdoor 
crews designed and implemented site specific temporary traffic 
management for each site including localised diversions.
Areas where surface dressing took place include Kilnamona, 
Doora, Ballyallia, Spancilhill, Cragnagower, Rathcruggaun and 
Ballyline. 
 
Footpath Repairs & Powerwashing
Ennis MD crews carried out footpath repair and remedial works 
this month. Works included full bay reinstatement to a defective 
footpath in Gort na Rí estate Ennis. Other works included 
Powerwashing of a number of areas including Friary carpark, 
Market area, Abbey St, Temple Gate car park and various road 
signs. 
Ennis Town Bus Service
Works have commenced with civil works associated with the 
Ennis Town Bus service this month. Glas Civil Engineering have 
been appointed as PSCS on behalf of the National Transport 
Authority and have been liaising and co-ordinating works 
through Ennis MD in terms of phasing plans, road opening 
licences, design elements and project programming in co-
ordination with local stakeholders. Works this month have 
taken place on the Clare Rd, Clon Rd, Francis Street and Bóthar 
Na Trócaire involving kerb re-alignment, installation of retention 
sockets, concrete footpaths, chamber ducting and structural 
bases to facilitate bus shelters. 
Road marking & upgrade of Disability parking 
spaces 
Ennis MD carried out upgrades to road markings in around the 
district area this month. Upgrades included refresh of centre

and parking enforcement marking i.e. double yellow lines

Ennis.
Separately, following the allocation of Ennis MD Councillor

compiled tender documents and following a procurement 
process, engaged the services of a specialist contractor to 
upgrade and refresh 43 disability parking spaces in around Ennis 
Town Centre.

Road Repairs & Drainage Works
Ennis MD carried out road surfacing repair works on Station 
Rd this month. These works followed the deterioration of the 
vehicle access/egress point to the HSE primary care centre 
on Station Rd. This entrance/exit also services a number of 
other businesses within the area. Input involved engagement 
with stakeholders in advance of co-ordinating the works. This 
involved online meetings, communication letters and site 
specific temporary traffic management plans. 
Drainage works were also carried out on Clonroadmore 
involving the construction of an upgraded soakpit drainage 
system. Works involved excavation and removal of excess silt 
and pipework and the installation of clean drainage stone, 
connecting pipework and associated reinstatement. 
 
Illegal Dumping & Oil Spills
There were a number of reports of illegal dumping this month. 
In co-ordination with the CCC Environment Department, Ennis 
MD assisted with clean ups following illegal dumping at areas 
including Clancy Park, Francis St and Waterpark Estate Ennis. 
These areas are proving to be litter/dumping blackspots and 
Ennis MD are working closely with the CCC Environment team 
and Ennis Garda Station on solving the issue going forward. 
 
Following reports of an oil spill in the Temple Gate area this 
month, Ennis MD responded by undertaking cleansing works 
in the area. Works involved implementing our oil spillage 
treatment bowser, application of specialised cleansing formula, 
road sweeping, and temporary traffic management to facilitate 
the works.

The Derelict Sites Team are committed to supporting and guiding 
property owners. Assistance is available to help identify practical 
solutions, access relevant schemes/grants and navigate the 
steps required to bring properties back into habitable use. The 
importance of timely action by the owner cannot be overstated. 
In parallel, owners are advised that the provisions of the Derelict 
Sites Act 1990 will be applied where necessary. This may result 
in a property being entered on the Derelict Sites Register, 
the imposition of a 7% annual levy, and/or consideration for 
compulsory purchase. By engaging early and taking proactive 
steps-through refurbishment, redevelopment or reuse - owners 
can reduce potential levy liabilities while making a positive 
contribution to the appearance and wellbeing of their community.
From Dereliction to Opportunity
Revitalising derelict and neglected properties is about far more 
than visual improvement - it is about unlocking the full potential 
of our communities. Clare County Council’s Derelict Sites staff 
together with the support of the local Councillors are leading this 
transformation with renewed focus, determination and a strong 
commitment to applying the Derelict Sites Act 1990 to its full 
extent.
Derelict and neglected buildings have long had a detrimental 
impact on the character, vitality and liveability of our towns, 
villages and rural hinterlands. Through a targeted, proactive 
and systematic approach, Clare County Council is addressing 
this challenge head-on. The number of properties actively 
being progressed under derelict sites legislation has increased 
significantly, rising from 303 at the end of 2025 to 378 today, 
ensuring that every appropriate legal mechanism is being utilised. 
143 of these are on the Derelict Sites Register.
This focused programme of work is helping to restore community 
pride and return valuable properties - particularly much-needed 
homes-to productive use. It builds on the progress achieved 
to date in rejuvenating communities across County Clare and 
supports the creation of attractive, vibrant places where people 
can live, work and enjoy their surroundings.
